reviewed_by: Codex review of provider-goal creation, stop, failure, refresh, and resume lifecycle
reason: Provider goals could only be created after the first message persisted a conversation, and cancelling a turn could leave the conversation's goal running because the turn had no goal_id or had already reached cancelled before the stop handler ran. The browser could also discard the final cancelled stream event while Stop aborted its viewer, leaving a terminal conversation visibly stuck on Waiting for provider. The selected backend tests cover atomic empty-conversation plus goal creation, explicit lifecycle revisions, live elapsed reads, and both linked and late-created goal cancellation. Focused frontend tests cover goal creation before a session exists, revision refresh behavior, and deterministic settlement of a live assistant bubble. The real-Core production LAN journey covers the operator path before the first message, first-turn linkage, stop-to-pause, authoritative idle state, removal of the stale provider wait, durable paired-browser reload, resume, accessibility, desktop, emulated mobile Chromium, and emulated mobile WebKit.
exclusions: No native tests because Rust and the desktop shell are unchanged. Harness goals, schedules, child-agent execution, unrelated provider transports, MCP execution, workspace behavior, and full suites are excluded. The selected real-Core journey uses the permanent desktop and 390 px Chromium/WebKit projects; 320 and 430 px profiles are excluded because this change reuses the existing responsive goal panel without CSS changes. A focused production build is performed separately from the test selection.
